page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an Arm-based general purpose instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It is powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 3.0 GHz, featuring 1 thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources consist of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 80 MB shared L3 cache. The server does not include dedicated GPUs. For local high-speed I/O, it integrates 1608 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage across 4 local SSD units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong capabilities in both memory subsystem throughput and data processing tasks. The instance placed in the top 10% for PassMark memory score (3247.82) and recorded top 25% performance in large-block uncached read bandwidth (314.24 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (120.6 GB/sec). General compute benchmarks like Geekbench showed strong results in single-core (1961.0) and multi-core (17040.0) tests, as well as text processing. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 32.37 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 221.45 GB/sec, placing both in the top quartile. Stress-ng compute scores and PassMark CPU scores remained in the average mid-range.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on the Neoverse-V2 core profile and specialized instruction sets. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via hardware AES, but x86-specific vector instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are naturally absent. The server provides dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores, ensuring predictable per-core execution times and reduced noisy-neighbor interference. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the inclusion of 1608 GB local NVMe SSD paired with high memory throughput yields high I/O density per dollar compared to attaching equivalent external persistent storage.

The workload profile suits memory-sensitive, I/O-intensive database and data processing tasks. Given its strong PassMark database operations metric (26262.23), sustained memory bandwidth, and high-speed local NVMe storage, the instance aligns well with distributed databases, transactional caches, high-throughput web serving, and ETL pipelines compiled for Arm64 architecture.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is a general purpose instance powered by an Arm-based ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, featuring 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs without multithreading. It provides 64 GB of system RAM alongside 1608 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage distributed across 4 local drives, with no onboard GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for PassMark memory performance, alongside top-quartile results in uncached memory bandwidth, single- and multi-core Geekbench metrics, and compression throughput. Stress-ng and general CPU metrics perform within average ranges. Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and high local I/O density, this instance offers solid cost efficiency for I/O-heavy operations, making it well-suited for transactional databases, Arm-native continuous integration, and data processing pipelines.
